elements.element: If the mutual-renewal branch is used, renewal requires agreement by both parties.

elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly requires a “written agreement.”

elements.element: If the automatic-renewal branch is used, each renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause permits renewal only by mutual written agreement and contains no automatic-renewal mechanism.

elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause contains no automatic-renewal mechanism.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no renewal price-increase cap. Requiring mutual agreement does not prevent the parties from agreeing to an increase above the stated cap.
The rendered clause instead provides that renewal may occur only by mutual written agreement.

elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause contains no automatic-renewal mechanism.

elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause contains no automatic-renewal mechanism.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no percentage cap on renewal price increases.

result.reason: The operative redline successfully replaces Licensor’s unilateral seven-year renewal option with renewal only by mutual written agreement, but it omits the preferred price cap. It also does not meet the fallback because it creates no automatic renewal and includes no 5% cap. The amendment leaves unrelated termination and payment provisions intact, but drafting quality is reduced by the retained malformed phrase “mutual written of the parties” and redundant renewal provisions.
